title: Maths reference: Year 8 Probability
summary: The words and methods from Year 8 Probability, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/probability-8 (see snippets/maths-algebra-7.json for the format; split from the strand courses' card files on 1 Nov 2026).

items.label: complementary events
items.hint: An event and its complement cover every outcome once. For 'at least one', count the outcomes with none and subtract from 1.
items.board:
widget: events
first: dice
event: a >= 5
complement: shown
items.shows: Roll 5 or 6 (A) and the other four outcomes (not A)

items.label: Venn diagram and two-way table
items.hint: Two yes/no properties make four groups: one only, both, the other only, neither. Each is a region of the Venn diagram and a cell of the table.
items.board:
widget: venn
labels: Sport, Music
counts: 12, 8, 5, 5
items.shows: The same 30 students as a Venn diagram and a two-way table

items.label: grid and tree diagram
items.hint: Two events make pairs: a grid or a tree lists every pair once, and the number of outcomes is the two counts multiplied. HT and TH are different outcomes.
items.board:
widget: events
first: red, blue, green
second: coin
names: Spinner, Coin
view: tree
event: b = H
items.shows: A spinner with three equal parts, then a coin: 6 outcomes, 3 of them heads

items.label: and, or, not
items.code: P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B)
items.hint: And is the overlap; or is one, the other or both; not A is everything outside A. Count each outcome once.
items.board:
widget: venn
labels: Dog, Cat
counts: 9, 4, 6, 11
event: a or b
items.shows: Dog or cat: everything inside the circles, 19 of 30

items.label: simulation
items.hint: Run many trials with random numbers (=RANDBETWEEN(1,6) is a dice) and compare the relative frequency with the probability. Short runs can be well off.
items.board:
widget: events
first: dice
second: dice
show: sum
event: s >= 10
items.shows: Two dice with a total of 10 or more chosen (6 of 36), ready to simulate
